newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ managed funds industry growth still tepid -IPAC.
newsitem.headline: NZ managed funds industry growth still tepid -IPAC.

text.p: New Zealand retail managed funds failed to attract new funds during the December quarter as high interest rates took their toll on investor enthusiasm, research company IPAC said on Wednesday.

The latest IPAC quarterly survey of growth trends shows that, despite improved returns, the net size of funds under management rose only modestly to $11.256 billion from $10.993 billion during the quarter.

"The average investor has been caught out by recent good returns. We believe this is due to a combination of lack of investment market understanding, focus on the short term and preoccupation with security rather than wealth accumulation," IPAC said in a statement.

The industry experienced a net investor funds outflow of -$19.3 million, down $142 million from the September quarter. IPAC said a major factor was a large advisory group's allocation of investor monies from public to private funds.
The personal superannuation fund sector continued to enjoy the highest level of retail investor support, receiving strong flows ($73 million) into diversified funds.
Negative funds flow was again evident in the unit trust and insurance bond sectors, both of which recorded only low funds growth.
"As was the case throughout 1996, low risk asset classes such as mortgages and cash remained relatively more popular," IPAC said.
